name: Extreme heat
value: Severe heatwave, Cape York to 19 Nov
summary: BoM severe heatwave warning for Queensland's Peninsula runs to 19 Nov; no deadly top-tier heatwave found
state: The Bureau of Meteorology's severe heatwave warning for Queensland's Peninsula and North Tropical Coast runs to 19 Nov, with Peninsula highs of about 37–43°C easing midweek; Weipa logged 41 straight days above 36°C to 15 Nov, its longest run on record (The Watchers). PAGASA forecast danger-level heat indices of 42–44°C at eight Philippine stations on 18 Nov (GMA News). A regional severe warning meets the Watch line; searches on 19 Nov found no deadly heatwave under top-tier warnings across a large population.
for_you: Travellers to northern Queensland should follow Bureau of Meteorology and Queensland Health heat advice and FCDO travel advice. Older people, infants and those with medical conditions are most exposed to heat stress.
rubric_hit: Watch: heatwave warnings across a major region (BoM severe heatwave, Peninsula, to 19 Nov); no deadly top-tier event for Alert

sources.title: The Watchers — Weipa hits 41 straight days above 36°C as severe heatwave grips Far North Queensland

why: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard globally, straining power grids, crops and health systems.
drivers: Heat domes, climate warming, season, humidity, urban heat islands.

rubric.alert: Deadly heatwave with top-tier official warnings across a large population.
rubric.watch: Heatwave warnings across a major region, or national temperature records.
rubric.normal: No major heatwaves affecting large populations.
